summary: resolvePublic now decodes the request path exactly once inside try/catch, rejects NUL bytes and backslashes, resolves against the absolute public directory and returns the path only if path.relative shows it is strictly inside public/, otherwise null; it never throws on request input. 16 tests added in test/serve.test.mjs covering E2E-1..3, the plan's Review Focus and both findings.

tests.name: relative root is resolved to an absolute path inside public/
E2E-2: traversal requests never resolve outside public/
F1: plain parent segments that escape return null
F1: percent-encoded parent segments and slashes that escape return null
F1: parent segments that stay inside public/ are accepted
F1: sibling directory sharing the public prefix is rejected
F1: the public directory itself is not a file to serve
F1: double-encoded traversal is decoded once and stays literal inside public/
E2E-3: % and %ZZ return null without throwing
F2: malformed or truncated escapes anywhere in the path return null
F2: malformed escape combined with traversal returns null, never a joined path
F2: non-string request paths return null without throwing

fixes.note: Resolve the candidate with path.resolve(path.resolve(root,'public'), './'+decoded) and accept it only when path.relative(base, candidate) is not '', not '..', does not start with '..'+path.sep and is not absolute; reject decoded paths containing NUL or backslash before resolving. The public directory itself ('/', '') returns null since it is not a file (stricter choice, added by me, flagged for the owner). resolvePublic is the only path-building function in src/ (grep for path.join/resolve/decodeURI), so there were no other sites to fix.
fixes.rule: Every filesystem path built from untrusted request input is accepted only after the final, fully resolved path is verified (by path.relative, not string prefix) to lie strictly inside the served base directory, and any input the filesystem could read differently from the check (NUL, backslash) is rejected.

fixes.note: decodeURIComponent is wrapped in try/catch and a failed decode returns null before any path is built; non-string request paths return null instead of throwing TypeError from decode/path. decodeURIComponent is the only decode call in src/.
fixes.rule: Untrusted request input is validated and decoded without letting any exception escape; any input that cannot be parsed is rejected (null) and never used to build a path.
